items.title: Agents Propose, Code Decides: An Autonomous Research Loop Framework to Build an Equity Alpha Model
items.claim: Agent-proposed predictors held their rank IC out of sample, but the hedged long-short retained only about half its expected Sharpe.

items.title: Agent Policy-Value Audit: Separating Transition Composition from Event Selection in Financial LLM Agents
items.claim: The agent's +15.2 bps/event gross deployment value is explained by transition composition, leaving selection value at -10.6 bps and no detectable skill.

items.title: Noisy Financial Machine Learning
items.claim: Against the panel historical mean rather than the zero forecast, only flexible nonlinear models show consistent gains, concentrated in small, value and illiquid stocks.

items.title: Large Language Models and Information Frictions in Corporate Bonds
items.claim: LLM-read earnings calls forecast rating migration a year ahead, and bond returns only where analysts disagreed, while post-earnings drift is not explained by it.

items.title: MintEval: Do LLMs Implement the Trading Strategy You Asked For? A Behavioural-Equivalence Benchmark for Natural-Language-to-Strategy Code
items.claim: A frontier model silently diverges from the requested strategy on 27.5% of tasks, and a recent LLM-judge benchmark accepts every such failure.

items.title: Mixture-of-Experts for Cryptocurrency Order Execution: Training Stability, Tail Risk, and Failure Modes
items.claim: Annealed exploration alone eliminates policy collapse in this environment, making expert partitioning unnecessary, and within-policy tail risk rises monotonically with K.
